:::{#exm-poisson-efficient}
#### The sample mean is efficient for Poisson data

For $\dsn{X} \siid \Pois(\rate)$,
the sample mean $\bar X$ is unbiased for $\rate$ ([the bias example](estimation.qmd#exm-bias-sample-mean)),
and, because $\Var{\Rvar_\iobs} = \rate$ for a Poisson variable,
$\Var{\bar X} = \rate / n$ ([the example on two estimators of a population mean](estimation.qmd#exm-mse-sample-mean)).
The expected information is $\einf(\rate) = n / \rate$ ([the Poisson information example](intro-MLEs.qmd#exm-information-poisson)), so

$$
\begin{aligned}
\frac{1}{\einf(\rate)}
&= \frac{1}{n / \rate}
&& \text{(substitute the expected information)}\\
&= \frac{\rate}{n}
&& \text{(reciprocal of a fraction)}\\
&= \Var{\bar X}
&& \text{(variance of the sample mean)}
\end{aligned}
$$

The sample mean attains the Cramér--Rao bound,
so it is an [efficient](#def-efficient) estimator of $\rate$.
It is also the maximum likelihood estimator ([the Poisson MLE example](intro-MLEs.qmd#exm-dist-mle-poisson)).
:::
